SMTO-EXE-0152 — SMTO can't move the mouse on that computer

GUID: 40f9503d-0ddd-5091-9ed0-893976a16860
Slug: ui-pointer-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO tried to click, drag or move the mouse in an app on the Gateway's computer, but that computer doesn't let SMTO control the mouse right now. Nothing was clicked.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to press the button or fill in the field by its name instead of clicking a spot on the screen. SMTO can often work an app's controls directly, which doesn't need mouse control at all.
  2. On a Mac, open System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility on the Gateway's computer and turn on the app that runs the Gateway. macOS blocks SMTO from moving the mouse until that permission is turned on.
  3. On a Linux computer, sign out and sign back in choosing an Xorg (X11) session instead of Wayland, then ask SMTO to try again. On Linux, SMTO can move the mouse only in X11 sessions; Wayland sessions don't allow it.
  4. On a Windows computer, make sure someone is signed in and the desktop is showing, not the lock or sign-in screen. Windows lets the Gateway move the mouse only inside a signed-in desktop session.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the click or drag, or does the same thing through the app's own controls, without showing this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway's computer. Don't turn off the computer's security or permission protections to force mouse control.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's Desktop UI service refused a pointer operation because live readiness did not report ui_pointer/ui_drag, or the platform adapter has no native pointer implementation.

What this means

  • Readiness lacked the pointer/drag capability or the adapter had no supported native pointer implementation. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Readiness lacked the pointer/drag capability or the adapter had no supported native pointer implementation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect pointer/drag readiness and platform support, preserving current permission and session boundaries.

How to fix it

  • Run ui.status on the selected Gateway and check pointer_input. Pointer fallback needs an X11 session with the XTEST extension on Linux (Wayland is not supported), Accessibility permission for the Gateway host on macOS (CGPreflightPostEventAccess), or an interactive desktop session on Windows; otherwise use semantic ui actions such as invoke, set_value or focus.
  • Use semantic accessibility actions. X11 XTEST or permitted native Windows/macOS input is required for pointer fallback.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use semantic accessibility actions. X11 XTEST or permitted native Windows/macOS input is required for pointer fallback.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended supported semantic action or explicitly permitted pointer path is available.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
